text:
Marta: quick notes from the 1pm 'routing & severity' workshop — threading here so we don't lose anything.
Marta: tl;dr: agreed on 3 immediate tweaks to reduce page noise and 2 infra items for the runtime.
Ashwin: thanks — I'll paste the raw watchlist export in a sec.
ops-bot: Incident BOT: Reminder — last night’s page spike (1864128000) showed >400 alerts in 15m, 72% were SEV3 auto-pages.
Jamie: reminder: customer impact recap: 3 customers saw degraded embeddings (long tail latency) for ~22m, but API success rate stayed >98%. no data loss.
Marta: correct — customer-facing impact existed but low severity. biggest problem was oncall overload.
SRE Lead: main workshop goal — reduce pages for noisy signals while preserving true-failure coverage.
Kelsey: one concrete: suppress pages on 4xx spikes from known client SDK churn. convert to SEV4 ticket by default, escalate if error-rate sustained >10m.
Marta: agreed. new policy: 4xx-spike -> ticket unless accompanied by >5% 5xx increase or latency P95 >2s for 5m.
Ashwin: I exported current routing rules. watchlist: 
```
- rule 101: token-service-5xx -> page, slack #platform-alerts
- rule 102: embeddings-latency-95 -> page, slack #platform-alerts
- rule 103: client-4xx-rate -> page, slack #platform-alerts
```
Ashwin: proposal: change rule 103 to ticket only, keep 101/102 paged.
Jamie: +1 for ticket change, but add a circuit-breaker: if 4xx persists and 5xx rises, auto-upgrade to page.
SRE Lead: we sketched an expression for that: "4xx_rate > X && (5xx_rate > Y || p95_latency > Z) for 5m" -> page.
Marta: action item: Ashwin to update rule 103 and add the escalation expression. Ashwin, can you also add a short description to the rule with examples of client churn so triage knows what to look for?
Ashwin: yep. I'll create RED-3421 and include examples + unit tests for the rule simulator.
ops-bot: PagerDuty: scheduled handoff - Marta -> Jamie at 18:00 UTC.
Marta: handoff note: if you get a page for embeddings-latency, check NVidia memory + KV-cache hit rate first. 2 quick scripts in /runbooks/embedding/diagnose.sh
Jamie: pinging @Kelsey for dashboard work — we need a compact dashboard that surfaces: p95, p99, kv-hit, queue-length, and recent model-variant rollouts. Current dashboard has too many panels.
Kelsey: will do a 'board-lite' by EOD. plan: reduce to top 6 KPIs + one sparkline per region. link in the ticket.
Marta: monitoring tuning decisions we committed to: 
- drop auto-page for client-4xx spikiness (convert to SEV4 ticket)
- add time-windowed escalation rule for sustained errors -> page
- add region-aware suppression during scheduled network maintenance windows
- add synthetic check to correlate if rollout tags coincide with latency spikes
Ashwin: region-aware suppression needs a list of maintenance CIDRs and a boolean flag in the router. we can use existing region-tag header.
Jamie: customer comms: we agreed not to send a blanket email, but to fire targeted notes to the 3 affected customers with the timeline and mitigations. I'll draft today.
SRE Lead: infra changes (short-term): 
1) throttle alert webhook fanout to prevent downstream alert storms (ops-bot was overwhelmed last night)
2) bump dedupe window for repeated identical alerts from 30s -> 3m for our high-frequency checks
Marta: both sound good. Ashwin, can you quantify estimated reduction in pages? rough numbers are fine.
Ashwin: estimate: dedupe window change -> ~45% fewer duplicate pages on noisy checks; ticket conversion for 4xx -> ~25% fewer pages. combined ~60% reduction in page volume for this class.
Kelsey: UX note: please add clear instructions in the alert description: what to run, what logs to check, and where to find runbooks. many alerts currently lack context.
Marta: agreed — mandatory alert template fields: symptoms, quick-runbook snippet, relevant dashboards, suggested first checks.
Jamie: question about 'page vs ticket' mapping for latency alerts: do we page when p95 > 3s for 2m, or p99 > 5s for 1m? workshop favoured p95 threshold for pages to avoid extreme tail noise.
SRE Lead: we decided: page if p95 > 2.5s for 3m OR p99 > 5s for 1m. that balances sensitivity and noise.
Ashwin: I'll codify thresholds in the routing rules and add unit tests. also will create a staging rule to run against replay data for one week.
Marta: replay is critical — we shouldn't deploy blind. schedule: staging rule today, run against replay, review Monday, prod deploy Tuesday morning.
ops-bot: Note: replay job scheduled: job-id=rb-2026-03-17-01, runs 24h of historical alerts across token-service.
Jamie: any objections to adding a 'silent hours' policy for low-usage windows where non-customer-impacting checks do not page? (eg 02:00-04:00 region local)
Kelsey: prefer careful — some customers in APAC are active at night. better: per-customer overrides. we can add per-customer oncall-sensitivity flags.
Marta: ok — add per-customer sensitivity meta; default behavior remains no silent hours.
SRE Lead: follow-up tasks (owners): 
- RED-3421 Ashwin: update rule 103 + unit tests + staging replay
- RED-3422 Kelsey: new 'board-lite' and dashboard links + embed on alert templates
- RED-3423 Jamie: customer comms drafts + list of affected accounts + send plan
- RED-3424 Marta: runbook template + update existing alerts to new template
Marta: I've added those to the post-incident board and assigned tentative due dates.
Ashwin: quick question — do we want ops-bot to annotate alert payloads with 'recent-deploy=true' when a rollout coincides? would help triage.
Jamie: yes please. make that a rule based on rollout tags from the deployment service.
Kelsey: also adding a tiny widget that shows last 10 deploys inline in the alert context panel.
Marta: final check — any security approvals needed for changing routing?
SRE Lead: no sensitive change; this is config-only. we will follow normal change control and include rollback plan.
Ashwin: implementing today: I'll update the rule and push to staging. I'll ping this thread when replay results finish.
ops-bot: Action: RED-3421 created by Ashwin.
Marta: thanks everyone. quick retrospective note: the handover last night was messy because the page volume buried context. the new requirement to include runbook snippet in alert will fix a lot of that.
Jamie: noted — i'll add a one-paragraph handoff template for oncall-to-oncall in the runbook.
Kelsey: putting a sticky reminder in #eng-oncall to follow these new rules during rota handovers.
SRE Lead: if no further comments, I'll close this workshop thread and we'll track progress in the RED tickets.
Marta: closing for now. will repost when staging replay is done. :white_check_mark:
